summary: The UK Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012 fixed tariff pays GBP110,000 (Level A18, ~USD139,700) for total loss of sight in both eyes (blindness), equating permanent total blindness to moderately severe brain damage in this statutory ladder.
label_raw: Loss of sight - both eyes (Level A18)
source_citation: Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012, Annex E Part A; gov.uk official guidance confirms loss of sight in both eyes = A18 = GBP110,000 https://www.gov.uk/guidance/criminal-injuries-compensation-scheme-injury-payments

summary: The UK Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012 fixed tariff pays GBP22,000 (Level A12, ~USD27,940) for total loss of sight in one eye - one fifth of the GBP110,000 paid for both eyes, a clean within-scheme single-vs-double concavity point.
label_raw: Loss of sight - one eye (Level A12)
source_citation: Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012, Annex E Part A; gov.uk official guidance confirms loss of sight in one eye = A12 = GBP22,000 https://www.gov.uk/guidance/criminal-injuries-compensation-scheme-injury-payments

summary: The UK Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012 fixed tariff pays GBP110,000 (Level A18, ~USD139,700) for moderately severe brain damage (serious disablement of physical/mental faculties requiring substantial dependence on care, marked impairment of intellect and personality).
source_citation: Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012, Annex E Part A; gov.uk official guidance confirms moderately severe brain damage = A18 = GBP110,000 https://www.gov.uk/guidance/criminal-injuries-compensation-scheme-injury-payments

summary: The UK Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012 fixed tariff pays GBP175,000 (Level A19, ~USD222,250) for substantially complete paraplegia (impairment of motor/sensory function of the lower extremities), one statutory step below the A20 cap.
source_citation: Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012, Annex E Part A; gov.uk official guidance confirms paraplegia 'substantially complete' = A19 = GBP175,000 https://www.gov.uk/guidance/criminal-injuries-compensation-scheme-injury-payments

summary: The UK Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012 fixed tariff pays GBP27,000 (Level A13, ~USD34,290) for permanent, seriously disabling mental injury (confirmed by psychiatrist/clinical psychologist) - the scheme's top pure-psychological tariff, a no-fault floor for severe permanent psychological suffering.
label_raw: Permanent mental injury, seriously disabling (Level A13)
source_citation: Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012, Annex E Part A; gov.uk official guidance confirms permanent mental injury 'seriously disabling' = A13 = GBP27,000 (moderately disabling = A11 = GBP19,000) https://www.gov.uk/guidance/criminal-injuries-compensation-scheme-injury-payments

summary: The UK Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012 fixed tariff sets the maximum single-injury payment at GBP250,000 (Level A20, ~USD317,500 at 1.27) - the statutory cap, awarded for the worst survivable injuries: quadriplegia/tetraplegia substantially complete to both upper and lower limb levels, and the most severe brain injury; a fixed, no-fault price far below court PSLA awards for the same injuries (~GBP493k JCG), showing strong concavity/cap behaviour in a statutory scheme.
source_citation: Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012, Annex E Part A; gov.uk official guidance confirms A20 = GBP250,000 = 'quadriplegia/tetraplegia substantially complete to both upper and lower limb levels' and most-severe brain injury https://www.gov.uk/guidance/criminal-injuries-compensation-scheme-injury-payments . NOTE: 'very serious brain injury' is the lower A19 (GBP175,000); only the most severe brain-injury category reaches A20.

summary: The UK Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012 fixed tariff floor is GBP1,000 (Level A1, ~USD1,270), the minimum award - covering e.g. disabling mental injury lasting 6 weeks up to 28 weeks, permanent slight loss of visual field, simple/minor fractures - the bottom anchor of the 25-level statutory suffering<->money scale that runs A1=GBP1,000 to A20=GBP250,000.
source_citation: Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012, Annex E; gov.uk official guidance confirms A1 = GBP1,000 is the lowest level and that 'disabling mental injury lasting 6 weeks or more up to 28 weeks' is an A1 (GBP1,000) injury https://www.gov.uk/guidance/criminal-injuries-compensation-scheme-injury-payments ; A1-GBP1,000 to A20-GBP250,000 range corroborated by cica-uk.co.uk and multiple secondary tables.

summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value amputation of both legs PSLA at GBP293,850-GBP344,150 (~USD373,200-USD437,000); midpoint ~USD405,000, sitting just below tetraplegia in the suffering ladder.
source_citation: Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (Apr 2024), Ch.7(I); bracket GBP293,850-GBP344,150 confirmed verbatim ('Loss of both legs') by Keoghs JCG v17 https://www.keoghs.co.uk/keoghs-insight/judicial-college-guidelines-version-17 . 'Above knee' qualifier dropped from label as the cited bracket is the 'loss of both legs' category.

summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value loss of one arm (amputation at the shoulder) PSLA at not less than ~GBP167,380 (~USD212,600), anchoring the suffering value of a single major limb amputation.
label_raw: Loss of one arm (amputation at the shoulder)
source_citation: Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (Apr 2024), Ch.6(B); 'amputation at the shoulder / loss of one arm not less than GBP167,380' confirmed across multiple amputation-claims sources (medicalaccidentlawyers.co.uk, compensationcalculatoruk.co.uk) https://www.compensationcalculatoruk.co.uk/list-of-compensation-payouts-in-the-uk/

summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value moderately severe brain injury (very serious disability, substantial dependence on care, marked intellectual/personality impairment) PSLA at GBP267,340-GBP344,150 (~USD339,500-USD437,000); midpoint ~USD388,000.
source_citation: Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (Apr 2024), Ch.3(A)(b); bracket GBP267,340-GBP344,150 reported by Mooneerams Solicitors https://www.mooneerams.com/blog/guide-to-traumatic-brain-injury-compensation-claims/ . Note: bracket sits between confirmed very-severe (GBP344,150-GBP493,000) and lower brain categories, consistent with JCG ladder; relied on a single secondary table for exact endpoints.

summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value very severe brain damage (little/no meaningful response to environment, double incontinence, need for full-time nursing care) PSLA at GBP344,150-GBP493,000 (~USD437,000-USD626,000); midpoint ~USD531,000 prices the suffering of catastrophic permanent brain injury just short of death.
source_citation: Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (Apr 2024), Ch.3(A)(a); 16th-ed GBP219,070-GBP403,990 uplifted to 17th-ed GBP344,150-GBP493,000 confirmed by Morton Fraser MacRoberts 2024 JCG summary https://www.mfmac.com/insights/personal-injury/judicial-college-guidelines-in-personal-injury-claims-2024/

summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value less severe PTSD (virtually full recovery within 1-2 years, only minor symptoms persisting) at GBP4,820-GBP9,980 (~USD6,100-USD12,700); midpoint ~USD9,400 - the floor of the PTSD suffering<->money ladder.
source_citation: Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (Apr 2024), Ch.4(B); bracket GBP4,820-GBP9,980 confirmed via WebSearch of JCG 17th-ed PTSD brackets and compensationcalculatoruk.co.uk https://www.compensationcalculatoruk.co.uk/list-of-compensation-payouts-in-the-uk/

summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value moderate PTSD (largely recovered, any continuing effects not grossly disabling) at GBP9,980-GBP28,250 (~USD12,700-USD35,900); midpoint ~USD24,000.
source_citation: Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (Apr 2024), Ch.4(B); bracket GBP9,980-GBP28,250 confirmed via WebSearch of JCG 17th-ed PTSD brackets and compensationcalculatoruk.co.uk https://www.compensationcalculatoruk.co.uk/list-of-compensation-payouts-in-the-uk/

summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value moderately severe PTSD (better prognosis with professional help but significant continuing disability) at GBP28,250-GBP73,050 (~USD35,900-USD92,800); midpoint ~USD64,000.

summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value severe PTSD (permanent effects preventing the victim from working or functioning at pre-trauma level) at GBP73,050-GBP122,850 (~USD92,800-USD156,000); midpoint ~USD124,000 - the cleanest pure psychological-suffering<->money anchor.
source_citation: Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (Apr 2024), Ch.4(B); bracket GBP73,050-GBP122,850 confirmed by multiple sources via WebSearch of JCG 17th-ed PTSD brackets and compensationcalculatoruk.co.uk https://www.compensationcalculatoruk.co.uk/list-of-compensation-payouts-in-the-uk/

summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value loss of sight in one eye WITH some reduced vision in the remaining eye at GBP117,150-GBP219,400 (~USD148,800-USD278,600); midpoint ~USD214,000. NOTE (corrected): this bracket is a two-eye injury (sight lost in one eye plus impairment of the other), NOT pure single-eye loss; total loss of sight in one eye with a sound other eye is only GBP54,880-GBP80,210, so the original 'half of losing both eyes / single-vs-double concavity' framing was wrong.
label_raw: Loss of sight in one eye with reduced vision in the remaining eye
source_citation: Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (Apr 2024), Ch.5; bracket GBP117,150-GBP219,400 confirmed by compensationcalculatoruk.co.uk JCG table https://www.compensationcalculatoruk.co.uk/list-of-compensation-payouts-in-the-uk/ as 'Sight loss in one eye and reduction of vision in remaining eye'. Connaught Law and comparecompensationclaims.com confirm pure single-eye loss is far lower (complete loss of sight in one eye GBP66,920-GBP80,210; total loss of one eye GBP54,880-GBP60,910), so the figure is right but the original label/concavity interpretation was wrong.

summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value tetraplegia/quadriplegia (complete paralysis of all four limbs) PSLA at GBP396,140-GBP493,000 (~USD503,000-USD626,000 at 1.27), the top non-fatal suffering bracket in English tort; midpoint ~USD565,000 prices the suffering of permanent total paralysis.
source_citation: Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (Apr 2024), Ch.2(A); bracket GBP396,140-GBP493,000 reported in Keoghs 'Judicial College Guidelines Version 17' https://www.keoghs.co.uk/keoghs-insight/judicial-college-guidelines-version-17 (confirmed verbatim)

summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value total blindness (loss of sight in both eyes) PSLA in the region of GBP327,940 (~USD416,000), pricing the permanent loss of all sight as suffering; sits just below the GBP493,000 'total blindness and deafness' category.
source_citation: Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (Apr 2024), Ch.5; 'in region of GBP327,940' per compensationcalculatoruk.co.uk JCG table https://www.compensationcalculatoruk.co.uk/list-of-compensation-payouts-in-the-uk/ and corroborated as 'GBP327,940-GBP354,260' by Connaught Law eye-injury guide. Some secondary sites quote a lower 'GBP268,720+' for total blindness; the GBP327,940 anchor is the better-corroborated figure.
